## Claim

The sequence $\{|X_n|\}$ is uniformly integrable.

## Proof

Recall the definition: a family $\{X_n\}$ is *uniformly integrable* (UI) if

$$\lim_{M\to\infty}\sup_n E\!\left[|X_n|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\right]=0.$$

By hypothesis, there exists a constant $C<\infty$ such that

$$\sup_n E|X_n|^{2+\sigma}\le C, \qquad \sigma>0.$$

**Key estimate.** On the event $\{|X_n|>M\}$ we have $|X_n|/M>1$, hence

$$|X_n|=|X_n|\cdot 1 \le |X_n|\cdot\left(\frac{|X_n|}{M}\right)^{1+\sigma}=\frac{|X_n|^{2+\sigma}}{M^{1+\sigma}}.$$

Therefore, pointwise on $\{|X_n|>M\}$,

$$|X_n|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\le \frac{|X_n|^{2+\sigma}}{M^{1+\sigma}}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\le \frac{|X_n|^{2+\sigma}}{M^{1+\sigma}}.$$

Taking expectations and using the hypothesis,

$$E\!\left[|X_n|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\right]\le \frac{E|X_n|^{2+\sigma}}{M^{1+\sigma}}\le \frac{C}{M^{1+\sigma}}.$$

This bound is independent of $n$, so taking the supremum over $n$,

$$\sup_n E\!\left[|X_n|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\right]\le \frac{C}{M^{1+\sigma}}.$$

Since $\sigma>0$, the exponent $1+\sigma>0$, and consequently

$$\lim_{M\to\infty}\frac{C}{M^{1+\sigma}}=0.$$

By the squeeze theorem,

$$\lim_{M\to\infty}\sup_n E\!\left[|X_n|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n|>M\}}\right]=0.$$

This is precisely the definition of uniform integrability. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** This is the standard "$p>1$ moment criterion" for UI: boundedness of a moment of order $p>1$ (here $p=2+\sigma>1$) implies uniform integrability. The argument only requires $E|X_n|^p$ uniformly bounded for some $p>1$; the specific value $p=2+\sigma$ is more than sufficient.

### PROOF COMPLETE
